newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says to close down six routes.
newsitem.headline: SAS says to close down six routes.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System on Tuesday said it planned to close down six routes which were not sufficiently profitable.
SAS also said it would lease out a Boeing 767 and three Fokker F28-1000s.
This would "lead to the disappearance of SAS's oldest F28's from the fleet", SAS said in a statement.

Among the affected destinations were Osaka, Japan routes from Stockholm and Copenhagen; Borlange, Sweden; Newcastle, England; Lyon, France; Minsk, Belarus; and Athens, Greece which are all non-stop flights to Copenhagen.

"It has been determined that these routes have too small a passenger base to allow them to operate with a profit. In addition, the number of flights between Stockholm and Umea will be reduced by 50 percent, to four flights per day," SAS said.
The Scandinavian carrier said it was evaluating some of the affected routes to see if they could be operated by an SAS partner or another airline in cooperation with SAS.
It also said it was negotiating with unions.
The Copenhagen-Minsk route would be cancelled next month because SAS did not get the number of passengers it had anticipated for this destination, it said.
The route to Osaka would be cancelled as of March 1. Changes in routes to Borlange, Newcastle, Lyon, France and Umea, Sweden would take effect on April 1.
The Athens route would be cancelled in the autumn of 1997.
The route cancellations would decrease production by two percent and thereby release capacity which could be used on other routes, it said.
"When the traffic program adjustments are complete, SAS anticipates a net production increase of three percent in 1997," the company said.
SAS said it would concentrate more on Finland and add frequencies on routes to Karlstad, Sweden and Dublin.
"More concentration will be placed on Finland, which is a growing market for SAS," the carrier said.
From April 1 the airline would fly to Oulu, Finland twice daily and double its frequencies to Finnish cities Tampere, Vaasa and Turku.
Positive development on the route between Copenhagen and Karlstad, Sweden, which was opened this year in March, allowed SAS to increase the frequency of the route to three from two.
It would add an afternoon/evening frequency to Dublin from Copenhagen, SAS said.
